slides.text:
Whole body lipid metabolism
Triglycerides are the primary form of lipids in the diet and make up nearly 90% of all lipid calories ingested.

Dietary lipids include triglycerides, phospholipids and sterols 

Recommendations for total lipid intake in adults - between 20 and 35% of calories for men and women aged over 30.

Transported around the body as triglycerides, cholesterol or free fatty acids

Note: Cholesterol intake has very little effect on blood cholesterol levels

Adipose tissue 
Loose connective tissue composed of fat cells known as adipocytes.

slides.topic: Whole-body Lipid Metabolism — Lipoproteins, Storage & Lipolysis — source 6
slides.text:
Adipose tissue

Cushions internal organs and insulates the body. Swell as they store fat and shrink when the fat is used for energy.

Not a passive energy depot but a dynamic “endocrine organ” that tightly regulates nutritional balance by means of a complex crosstalk of adipocytes with their microenvironment and other tissues by various hormonal/chemical signals. 


Dysfunctional adipose tissue, particularly as observed in obesity, is characterized by adipocyte hypertrophy, macrophage infiltration, impaired insulin signalling, and insulin resistance. 

Results in the release of inflammatory adipokines and excessive amounts of free fatty acids that promote ectopic fat deposition and lipotoxicity in muscle, liver, and pancreatic β cells.

Lipoprotein lipase

Rate limiting enzyme for hydrolysis and removal of circulating triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (TRL)

Very important role in energy homeostasis

Activated by insulin
